Assume that the kernel matrix of the combined family $(x^*, x)$, indexed by $\tau \sqcup \nu$, is positive semidefinite, and let $\sigma^2 > 0$. Let $V$ be a measurable random vector…
nodes.title: The Gaussian-process posterior

nodes.summary: Let $k : X \times X \to \mathbb{R}$ be a kernel and $x = (x_j)_{j \in \nu}$ a finite family of inputs whose kernel matrix $K = (k(x_i, x_j))_{i, j \in \nu}$ is positive semidefinite. Then for every $\sigma^2 > 0$ the matrix $K + \sigma^2 I$ has nonzero determinant, so it is invertible.
nodes.title: Regularized kernel matrices are invertible

nodes.summary: For a kernel $k : X \times X \to \mathbb{R}$, a real number $\sigma^2$, test inputs $x^* = (x^*_i)_{i \in \tau}$ and training inputs $x = (x_j)_{j \in \nu}$, the joint covariance of $k$, $\sigma^2$, $x^*$ and $x$ equals $K + D$, where $K$ is the kernel matrix of the combined family $(x^*, x)$ indexed by $\tau \sqcup \nu$ and $D$ is the diagonal matrix with entry $0$ at each test index and $\sigma^2$ at each…
nodes.title: The joint covariance as a kernel matrix plus noise

nodes.summary: Let $k : X \times X \to \mathbb{R}$ be a kernel, let $x^* = (x^*_i)_{i \in \tau}$ and $x = (x_j)_{j \in \nu}$ be families of test and training inputs, and let $\sigma^2 \ge 0$. If the kernel matrix of the combined family $(x^*, x)$, indexed by $\tau \sqcup \nu$, is positive semidefinite, then the joint covariance of $k$, $\sigma^2$, $x^*$ and $x$ is positive semidefinite.
nodes.title: The joint covariance is positive semidefinite

nodes.summary: The joint prior covariance of the test values `f(x*)` and the noisy training targets `y = f(x) + ε`, `ε ~ N(0, σ² I)`: `[[K(x*, x*), K(x*, x)], [K(x, x*), K(x, x) + σ² I]]`.
nodes.title: Joint prior covariance in Gaussian-process regression

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
